passages.source_passage: The Mbalendo Home Care Collective was founded in 2011 to support people living with HIV in the hill villages of Kasenzi District. Our 46 trained caregivers currently visit roughly three hundred households each month, delivering adherence counselling, basic wound care and referrals to the district clinic. A 2022 household survey found that 38% of clients had missed at least one clinic appointment in the previous quarter, most often because of transport costs. Caregivers do not receive a stipend, and many travel more than ten kilometres on foot between visits. Without additional support, the Collective cannot extend visits to the newly mapped settlements along the Rufala River, where an estimated 120 people are enrolled in treatment but have never received a home visit.

passages.source_passage: At the midpoint of the Tumaini Playgroup Network's three-year cycle, evaluators from Lakeshore Learning Associates visited 24 of the 40 community playgroups in Ombeni Ward between March and May 2023. Attendance has grown steadily, with an average of 18 children aged three to five present at each session, up from eleven at baseline. Caregivers reported that children now spend more time on counting and storytelling games at home. However, fewer than half of the playgroups had a dedicated shaded space, and sessions were frequently cancelled during the rains. The evaluation did not find meaningful differences in language scores between boys and girls. Facilitators asked for refresher training, noting that no follow-up visits from coordinators had taken place since the launch workshop.

passages.source_passage: Farmers in the Venda Plateau grow maize and beans on plots averaging 1.2 hectares, and most depend entirely on a single rainy season. Since 2019, the Green Furrow Trust has run 32 farmer field schools, each bringing together about twenty-five farmers to test practices such as mulching, intercropping and early planting on shared demonstration plots. Participating households reported maize yields 27% higher than neighbouring non-members in the 2022 harvest. Yet the schools have not reached the plateau's eastern valleys, where roads wash out for months at a time. Women make up 61% of members, but few hold title to the land they farm, which limits their access to credit and inputs.

passages.source_passage: Before the first meeting, remind the group that each Pamoja Savings Circle should have between 15 and 25 members who live close enough to attend every week. Members buy shares at a value they agree together, usually 500 shillings per share, and no one may buy more than five shares at a single meeting. The cash box must have three padlocks, with keys held by three different members who are not on the management committee. Loans are repaid with a monthly service charge of 10%, and the full cycle normally lasts twelve months before the share-out. Do not handle the group's money yourself, even if members ask you to count it. Your role is to guide the process, not to manage the funds.

passages.source_passage: Following two consecutive failed harvests in 2021 and 2022, food insecurity in the lowland districts of Marrabé has reached levels not seen in a decade. A rapid assessment by the Horizonte Relief Alliance found that 42% of households were eating only one meal a day, and nearly a third had sold livestock to buy grain. Local markets continue to function, and traders reported no shortages of staple foods, which makes cash a more efficient response than in-kind distribution. Our pilot transfer of 1,800 meticais per month reached 650 households last year. Recipients did not use the money for alcohol or other non-essential goods, according to post-distribution monitoring, and most spent it on maize flour, beans and school fees.

passages.source_passage: During the 2023 school year, the Becas Luz de Montaña programme supported 214 girls attending lower and upper secondary schools in the highland municipalities of San Telmo and Las Ceibas. Retention remained strong: 93% of scholars completed the year, compared with roughly two thirds of girls in the same grades across the department. Twenty-eight scholars graduated in November, and eleven of them have enrolled in teacher-training or technical institutes. Not every challenge was resolved. Rising bus fares meant that some girls from the most remote aldeas could not attend classes regularly during the coffee harvest, and the stipend was not increased to cover the gap. We are grateful to the Fundación Arroyo Claro for its continued partnership.

passages.source_passage: Board members will recall that the Assiette Pleine programme expanded to 58 primary schools in the Koulimba region in January 2024. Cooks now serve a hot midday meal of millet, cowpeas and fortified oil to approximately 17,000 pupils on every school day. Head teachers at participating schools report that average daily attendance rose from 71% to 84% over the first term. Deliveries from the central warehouse were delayed twice in February, and nine schools did not serve meals for up to a week. Procurement from local farmers' cooperatives now accounts for one third of all grain purchased. The management team does not recommend further expansion until a second storage depot is operational.

passages.source_passage: Since the last board meeting in September, the Kindred Paths Counselling Service has completed 1,140 individual sessions across its four drop-in centres in Harlow Vale and the surrounding townships. Waiting times for a first appointment have fallen to an average of nine days, down from three weeks in the spring. Our lay counsellors are supervised fortnightly by two clinical psychologists seconded from the district hospital. We have not secured funding to continue the evening support group for bereaved parents beyond March, and attendance there has doubled since it opened. No serious safeguarding incidents were reported this quarter. Staff wellbeing remains a concern, with three counsellors taking extended leave for burnout.

passages.source_passage: In the rural counties of Brenmoor and Tallis Ford, there is roughly one practising lawyer for every 40,000 residents, and none of the county courts offers a duty legal advice desk. Since 2020, the Open Gate Justice Project has trained 36 community paralegals to help residents resolve disputes over land, inheritance and unpaid wages. In the past year alone, paralegals handled 2,300 cases, and 58% were resolved through mediation without going to court. Many clients are widows who were not told of their right to inherit their husbands' property. Demand far exceeds capacity: paralegals currently cover only seven of the region's nineteen sub-counties.

passages.source_passage: In the char islands of Nilganj Upazila, fewer than four in ten births take place in a health facility, and many mothers deliver at home with only a relative present. The Shishu Alo Outreach Project, launched in 2021, sends teams of two community midwives by boat to 22 island settlements on a fixed monthly schedule. Last year the teams provided 1,560 antenatal check-ups and referred 214 women with danger signs to the Upazila Health Complex. Monsoon flooding remains the main barrier, and boats did not operate for six weeks in July and August. Newborn deaths have not been systematically recorded on the islands, so the project's impact on neonatal mortality cannot yet be measured.
